source.book: The Art and Science of Technical Analysis
source.author: Adam Grimes

conventions: stop and limit entries mechanized as bar-close then next-bar-open; every tunable constant is a parameter; long side only in pseudocode, sides field says mirrored/same; price-level conditions rejected (shift test); higher-timeframe reasoning approximated by a longer lookback on the same bars

candidates.name: CloseBeyondKeltnerBand
candidates.quote: modified Keltner channels set 2.25 multiples of the Average True Range (ATR) around a 20-period exponential moving average
candidates.description: Primitive: close closes above the upper Keltner band (EMA of length L plus M times ATR of length L); mirrored below the lower band on the short side. Grimes's core indicator, used throughout the chapter as the sign of strong momentum and as the climax/free-bar reference.

complexity.reason: needs an EMA and an ATR, both cross-bar state

notes: Distinct from the catalog's KeltnerChannelCross (a state-machine cross of a plain-Average band); this is a bare close-beyond-band comparison against an EMA band, matching how Grimes actually uses it in this chapter (impulse legs, free bars, climaxes).

candidates.name: FreeBar
candidates.quote: it is extremely unusual to see bars that are completely outside the Keltner channels, called free bars; the presence of these bars is another sign of potential climax
candidates.description: A bar entirely outside the Keltner band: for a bull free bar the bar's low sits above the upper band; mirrored (high below lower band) for a bear free bar.

complexity.reason: shares G03-01's EMA/ATR band

candidates.name: ConsecutiveFreeBarCount
candidates.quote: an accelerated trend rate, large range bars, manyfree bars (bars with a low above the upper channel), and a subsequent collapse
candidates.description: Count of free bars (G03-02) within the last N bars meets or exceeds a threshold -- Grimes's 'many free bars' climax marker.

complexity.reason: a CountIF over a band comparison, both cross-bar state

notes: freeBarThreshold and freeBarLookback are the mining agent's defaults; the book gives no number ('not uncommon' four or five times average volume, but no bar count for the free-bar run).

candidates.name: LargeRangeBarVsAverage
candidates.quote: the range of the bars in the blow-off becomes much larger than previous bars as the trend steepens and the bars pull away from the average
candidates.description: Bar range is much larger than the recent average bar range -- one of Grimes's climax markers.

complexity.reason: a window average of bar range

candidates.name: AcceleratedTrendRate
candidates.quote: Note the classic signs of a buying climax in this example: an accelerated trend rate, large range bars
candidates.description: The rate of the trend (price change per bar) over a short recent window is a multiple of the rate over an equal, older window -- the trend is steepening.

complexity.reason: compares two lagged price-difference rates, no persistent state but two offset reads

notes: Grimes gives 'rate' no formula; this reduces price/time slope to a ratio of two displacement rates. Distance rather than magnitude, so sides is 'same' (abs()), unlike a directional momentum test.

candidates.name: ConsecutiveClosesAtBarExtremeRun
candidates.quote: many more bars close at or near their high in a buying climax and on their low in a selling climax
candidates.description: For N consecutive bars, the close sits in the top fraction of each bar's own range (bull) -- a climax/exhaustion sign that also recurs in the chapter's 'character of trend legs' checklist.

complexity.reason: a persistent all-of-N-bars check

candidates.name: ClimaxVolumeSpike
candidates.quote: It is not uncommon to see bars that trade four or five times the average volume for the instrument
candidates.description: Bar volume exceeds a multiple of its own recent average volume -- a climax marker; not a price-level test so it passes the shift test.

complexity.reason: a window average of volume

candidates.name: ClimaxAfterMultipleTrendLegsComposite
candidates.quote: Usually come after two or more trend legs in the same direction. Show an acceleration in the direction of the previous trend.
candidates.description: Composite climax condition: two or more prior trend legs in the same direction (needs leg/pivot counting, a design decision), plus acceleration, large range bars, free bars, and closes bunched at the bar extreme. Grimes's summary checklist for identifying a climax/exhaustion top or bottom.
candidates.pseudocode: priorTrendLegCount >= 2 AND (G03-05 OR G03-04) AND (G03-02 OR G03-06)

complexity.reason: leg counting needs a swing/pivot detector and a design decision for what counts as a 'trend leg'; the component tests are otherwise mechanical

notes: Grimes also notes climaxes 'vary in significance' and are rare mid-range (usually at a significant new high/low) -- both are further design decisions left for authoring.

candidates.name: AvoidPullbackAfterClimax
candidates.quote: Do not enter pullbacks following potential climaxes.
candidates.description: Block with-trend pullback entries for N bars after a climax condition (G03-08) fires.

complexity.reason: a persistent bars-since counter keyed to G03-08

candidates.name: SharpCountertrendMomentumBreaksTrend
candidates.quote: this pullback completely broke the established trend pattern, and spiked the MACD to a sharp new low, which is not consistent with an intact uptrend
candidates.description: A large-range bar against the trend direction during a pullback (mirrors G03-04, directional) -- the trend is considered broken; block further with-trend entries until a new impulse confirms the trend again. Same mechanics apply to the 'wrong side' pullback-failure pattern described later in the chapter (page 89-90).

complexity.reason: a window average plus a directional bar test

candidates.name: ParabolicDistanceFromEma
candidates.quote: the bars pull away from the average; this is a reflection of expanded volatility, specifically intraday volatility
candidates.description: Close is more than K ATRs above (long) / below (short) its own EMA -- measures how far price has pulled away from the moving average, a parabolic-extension gauge.

complexity.reason: an EMA and an ATR

candidates.name: MomentumIndicatorNewExtreme
candidates.quote: the fast line of the MACD registered a new momentum high
candidates.description: Primitive: a momentum indicator (Grimes's modified MACD fast line, or a generic EMA-difference oscillator) reaches a new N-bar extreme (high in an uptrend, low in a downtrend) relative to its own recent history.
candidates.pseudocode: mom(close, fastLen, slowLen)[0] >= highest(mom(close, fastLen, slowLen), momLookback)[1]

complexity.reason: an EMA-difference oscillator plus a rolling highest/lowest of its own history

notes: Grimes's exact modified-MACD / 3-10-oscillator formula is defined precisely in Chapter 7 / Appendix B; this chapter only uses the concept 'a new momentum high or low relative to recent history'. fastLen/slowLen guessed at the book's namesake 3/10 oscillator per the mining brief -- confirm against the appendix chapter when mined.

candidates.name: MomentumDivergenceAtNewPriceExtreme
candidates.quote: At the point marked B, the market made a new high but the momentum indicator did not. This is a momentum divergence
candidates.description: Price makes a new N-bar high (low) but the momentum indicator (G03-12) does not make a concurrent new extreme -- a momentum divergence.
candidates.pseudocode: close[0] >= highest(close, lookback)[1] AND NOT (mom(close,fastLen,slowLen)[0] >= highest(mom(close,fastLen,slowLen), momLookback)[1])

complexity.reason: two rolling-extreme comparisons and a negation

candidates.name: AvoidPullbackAfterDivergence
candidates.quote: suggests that long trades should not be entered on the next pullback
candidates.description: Block with-trend pullback entries when the most recent new price extreme was accompanied by a momentum divergence (G03-13).

complexity.reason: a persistent bars-since counter keyed to G03-13

candidates.name: PullbackFollowsStrongImpulseFilter
candidates.quote: trade only pullbacks that are preceded by significant momentum in the direction of the trend
candidates.description: Only take with-trend pullback entries when the impulse leg preceding the pullback was accompanied by G03-12 (momentum indicator registering a new extreme) within a recent lookback.

complexity.reason: a persistent bars-since counter keyed to G03-12

candidates.name: SimplePullbackPrimitive
candidates.quote: A pullback is a countertrend movement ... in a trend that usually leads to another price movement in the direction of the original trend
candidates.description: Primitive: a pullback is a run of bars moving against the established trend direction following an impulse leg. Approximated here as consecutive lower closes with no new trend-direction extreme; downstream candidates refer to this by id rather than redefining it.
candidates.pseudocode: close[0] < close[1] AND close[0] < highest(close, pullbackBars)[1]

complexity.reason: true pullback identification needs swing-pivot detection to mark the start and end of the countertrend leg; this is a consecutive-bar/no-new-extreme proxy

candidates.name: ComplexPullbackTwoLegged
candidates.quote: the complex pullback, which is a standard pullback followed by a failed attempt to resume the original trend. When this attempt fails and rolls over, the pullback puts in a second leg against the larger trend
candidates.description: After a pullback (G03-16) and a failed resumption attempt (price tries but fails to make a new trend-direction extreme), the market makes a second countertrend leg beyond the first pullback's extreme -- a complex ('two-legged') pullback.
candidates.pseudocode: pivotLow2 < pivotLow1 AND priceAttemptedNewHighBetween(pivot1, pivot2) AND thatAttemptFailed

complexity.reason: needs swing-pivot detection over a variable-length window plus a fail/resume state machine

notes: Also called a 'two-legged pullback'; Elliott's alternation rule (simple/complex pullbacks alternate through an extended trend) is noted by Grimes but is not itself a bar-level test -- left as a note for the authoring pass, not a separate candidate.

candidates.name: MeasuredMoveObjectiveTarget
candidates.quote: A rough profit target for the follow-through leg ... is the so-called measured move objective (MMO), which assumes that the CD leg ... will approximately equal the length of the AB leg
candidates.description: Profit target for the trend-resumption leg (CD) equals the length of the prior impulse leg (AB), projected from the pullback's extreme (C).
candidates.book_order_type: limit at target (mechanized as close-and-next-open once reached, per convention)

complexity.reason: needs swing-pivot detection to locate points A, B, and C

notes: Grimes explicitly treats this as a rough guideline, not exact; also usable as an entry-area target for the second leg of a complex pullback (G03-17).

candidates.name: ThreePushesPattern
candidates.quote: three pushes, which appears on a price chart as three drives to a new high or low after a somewhat extended trend ... In the best examples, the third push breaks a trend line drawn across pushes one and two
candidates.description: Three successive drives to a new trend extreme, roughly symmetric in time and price, spaced more closely together than the trend's typical prior swing spacing; the third push often breaks the trend line connecting pushes 1 and 2 -- a short-term climax/exhaustion warning.
candidates.pseudocode: push1, push2, push3 = successive swing extremes in trend direction; abs(push2-push1) approx abs(push3-push2) AND barsBetween(push2,push3) < barsBetween(push1,push2) AND priceCrossesTrendLine(push1,push2)

complexity.reason: needs swing-pivot detection and trend-line projection from those pivots

notes: Heavily covered already by the Brooks-derived ThreePush* family in the catalog; recorded here for completeness per the mining brief.

candidates.name: RetracementDepthWithinExpectedBand
candidates.quote: expect retracements to terminate at about 50 percent of the preceding setup leg ... look for terminations somewhere in the 25 to 75 percent range
candidates.description: Pullback depth, as a fraction of the preceding setup leg's length, is expected to fall within a 25-75% band; used to flag pullbacks that are unusually shallow or unusually deep relative to that band.
candidates.pseudocode: retracementFraction = (pointB - lowSoFar) / (pointB - pointA); retracementFraction >= minFraction AND retracementFraction <= maxFraction

complexity.reason: needs swing-pivot detection to locate the setup leg's endpoints

candidates.name: RidingTheKeltnerBandNoPullback
candidates.quote: they will press against the upper channel and slide along that band as the market grinds higher
candidates.description: An extremely strong trend where price repeatedly closes at or beyond the Keltner band for consecutive bars without pulling back to the EMA -- a 'riding the band' condition identifying trends offering no tradable pullback.

complexity.reason: a CountIF over G03-01's band test

notes: Grimes also warns these trends produce occasional large spikes against the trend, making risk hard to define -- left as a note for the authoring pass rather than a separate rule.

candidates.name: PullbackLowerActivityFilter
candidates.quote: they are generally periods of lower activity compared to trend legs
candidates.description: Valid pullback bars should show a smaller average range than the average range of the preceding impulse leg's bars.

complexity.reason: needs pivot detection to separately identify pullback-leg bars vs. the preceding impulse-leg bars

candidates.name: FlatPullbackStallsIntoRange
candidates.quote: the market begins what looks like a good pullback but then there is simply no move out of that pullback. Instead, the market goes into a flat range
candidates.description: After a pullback of N bars, price has failed to make a new trend-direction extreme and recent bar ranges have contracted to a narrow band -- the pullback has stalled into a range; exit or avoid new with-trend entries.
candidates.pseudocode: barsSince(pullbackStart) > stallBars AND NOT newExtremeSince(pullbackStart) AND average(high-low, recentBars) < tightMultiple*average(high-low, priorBars)
candidates.book_order_type: market at next open once flagged, per convention

complexity.reason: needs a pullback-start pivot plus a persistent no-new-extreme flag

candidates.name: PivotTargetForPullbackTrade
candidates.quote: the pivot high or low (in an uptrend or a downtrend, respectively) of the setup leg is an ideal target and should be considered the first, most conservative profit target for any pullback trade
candidates.description: First, conservative profit target for a pullback trade: the pivot extreme of the setup leg preceding the pullback (the prior swing high in an uptrend).
candidates.book_order_type: limit at prior pivot (mechanized as close-and-next-open once reached)

complexity.reason: needs swing-pivot detection

candidates.name: FailureAtConsolidationLowReversalEntry
candidates.quote: There was no momentum and no selling conviction below the level. Within two days, the market was solidly back above the consolidation
candidates.description: Price breaks decisively below a pullback/consolidation's low, but within a few bars closes back above that same low -- a failed breakdown that offers a with-trend long entry at a favorable price.
candidates.pseudocode: anyOf(k in 1..failBars, low[k] < consolidationLow) AND close[0] > consolidationLow
candidates.book_order_type: market at close, next-bar-open fill per convention

complexity.reason: needs a defined consolidation low, itself a swing/window construct

candidates.name: DowUptrendHigherHighsHigherLows
candidates.quote: An uptrend is a pattern of successively higher pivot highs (HHs) and higher pivot lows (HLs) ... if a market is only making higher highs, but is not also clearly holding higher lows, the buyers are not solidly in control
candidates.description: Primitive trend-state definition: the market is in an uptrend when the most recent confirmed swing high is above the prior swing high AND the most recent confirmed swing low is above the prior swing low (mirrored for downtrend).

complexity.reason: requires a pivot/swing detector with a design decision for pivot strength/lookback before a state machine can track HH/HL sequences

candidates.name: DowTrendChangeUncertainThenConfirmed
candidates.quote: if the market falls short of the previous pivot high, the trend status becomes uncertain ... The trend change is actually confirmed only when price trades through the last pivot low, marking a lower low
candidates.description: Trend status becomes 'uncertain' when a with-trend leg fails to make a new extreme past the prior pivot; the downtrend is only confirmed once price also breaks the last pivot low -- Dow theory's first trend-change pattern.
candidates.pseudocode: swingFailedToExceedPriorPivotHigh AND (state == UNCERTAIN) AND close[0] < priorPivotLow -> state = DOWNTREND

complexity.reason: a multi-stage pivot state machine (up / down / uncertain) needing a swing detector

candidates.name: DowTrendChangeSharpReversalTakesOutPivot
candidates.quote: prices retreat so aggressively from the highs that they take out the previous pivot low ... the trend change is not confirmed until the market again takes out the previous low
candidates.description: A sharp reversal takes out the previous pivot low directly from a new swing high (one swing shows both a higher high and a lower low); the trend change is confirmed only after the following rally fails below the prior high and price again breaks the prior low.
candidates.pseudocode: swingHigh0 > priorSwingHigh AND swingLow0 < priorSwingLow -> (rally1 < swingHigh0) AND close[0] < swingLow0 -> confirmedChange

complexity.reason: a multi-stage pivot state machine

candidates.name: MovingAverageSlopeTrendFilter
candidates.quote: One of the simplest trend indicators used by traders is the slope of a single moving average
candidates.description: The market is in an uptrend (downtrend) when a single moving average of a chosen length is rising (falling) -- its current value is above (below) its value N bars ago.

complexity.reason: an average plus a lagged self-comparison

notes: Grimes notes many false signals when the average is flat, suggesting an optional undefined/dead zone around zero slope; left as a parameter (slopeThreshold) for the authoring pass rather than a separate candidate.

candidates.name: ShrinkingSwingLengthsWarning
candidates.quote: the trend is running out of steam occurs when successive upswings are shorter relative to previous upswings
candidates.description: Successive with-trend swings become progressively shorter than the swings preceding them -- an early warning that the trend is losing momentum.

complexity.reason: needs swing-pivot detection and a running series of swing lengths

candidates.name: FirstOversizedCounterSwingWarning
candidates.quote: the first downswing in an uptrend that is longer than the preceding upswing ... this swing can indicate a distinct change of character in the market ... it may even set up a potential countertrend short on the next bounce
candidates.description: The first countertrend swing that exceeds the preceding with-trend swing (in price or in bars) -- a trend-character warning and a possible countertrend setup on the next bounce.

complexity.reason: needs swing-pivot detection to compare consecutive swing lengths

candidates.name: SwingLengthExceedsAverageMultipleWarning
candidates.quote: if, after several swings in the same direction, a swing emerges that is two to three times the length of the average swing, this may indicate an overextended market and a possible climax
candidates.description: The current with-trend swing's length is 2-3x the average of recent swings -- an overextension/climax warning.

complexity.reason: needs swing-pivot detection and a rolling average of swing lengths

candidates.name: LargeBarNearLegEndWarning
candidates.quote: very large bars near the end of a swing can indicate exhaustion or climax, which will usually be obvious on the lower time frame
candidates.description: A large-range bar (G03-04) occurring near the end of a trend leg (rather than early or mid-leg) is an exhaustion/climax warning, distinct from a large bar that just signals conviction.
candidates.pseudocode: (high[0]-low[0]) > rangeMultiple*average(high-low, rangeLookback) AND barsSince(legStart) >= legLength - nearEndBars

complexity.reason: reuses G03-04's window average; the leg-position test needs a defined leg start

candidates.name: GapDoesNotFillContinuationSignal
candidates.quote: Are there gaps up that do not fill on a daily chart?
candidates.description: An opening gap in the trend direction that is not filled (price never trades back through the pre-gap close) within N bars -- a sign of strong conviction/continuation.
candidates.pseudocode: open[0] > close[1] AND lowest(low, fillLookback) > close[1]

complexity.reason: a rolling lowest/highest window since the gap

candidates.name: HigherTimeframeTrendAlignmentFilter
candidates.quote: the uptrend on the daily chart is likely to terminate suddenly as the weekly chart reasserts control and the downtrend on that time frame resumes
candidates.description: Only take with-trend pullback entries on the trading timeframe when a higher-timeframe proxy (a much longer-lookback moving-average slope on the same bars) agrees in direction; avoid entries counter to that higher timeframe.

complexity.reason: 'higher time frame trend' is a genuine design decision even once approximated by a longer lookback -- how much longer, and how to reconcile conflicting timeframes, needs a choice by the authoring pass

notes: Higher timeframe approximated per the mining brief by a longer lookback on the same bars rather than a true multi-timeframe read.

candidates.name: StandardTrendLineDefinition
candidates.quote: Standard uptrend lines are drawn between higher lows in an uptrend; the standard downtrend line is a line drawn between lower highs in a downtrend
candidates.description: Primitive: a standard trend line connects two successive swing lows in an uptrend (swing highs in a downtrend); the line's projected value at the current bar is a potential support (uptrend) or resistance (downtrend) level.

complexity.reason: needs swing-pivot detection and a linear projection from two pivots

notes: Extensive existing coverage in the Brooks-derived corpus (TrendLine*, ChannelLine*); recorded here for completeness.

candidates.name: ParallelChannelTakeProfitZone
candidates.quote: if you are long in an uptrend and prices rise to the upper parallel trend line, it probably makes sense to be slightly defensive and to take some profits
candidates.description: Price reaches the upper parallel trend line (a trend line anchored to the standard trend line's opposite-side pivots) -- take partial profits.
candidates.book_order_type: limit at the channel line (mechanized as close-and-next-open once reached)

complexity.reason: needs the parallel-channel projection built on G03-36's pivots

candidates.name: ParallelChannelBreakoutAcceleration
candidates.quote: it is a strong vote of confidence from the dominant group in the market ... and often leads to a new trend that proceeds at a faster rate
candidates.description: Price closes decisively beyond the parallel channel line -- a stronger, faster new trend phase; a bullish continuation signal rather than a fade opportunity.
candidates.book_order_type: market at next open once broken, per convention

complexity.reason: needs the parallel-channel projection built on G03-36's pivots

candidates.name: MicroTrendLineReclaimEntry
candidates.quote: wait for the market to recover back above the trend line, and then to buy with a stop just under the low of the bar that broke the trend line
candidates.description: A very short (1-3 bar) trend line inside a pullback is briefly violated, then price recovers back above it within a few bars -- the recovery is itself the entry trigger, with a stop just beyond the extreme of the break.
candidates.pseudocode: low[k] < microTrendLineValue(k) for some recent k AND close[0] > microTrendLineValue(0)
candidates.book_order_type: buy stop on recovery above the micro trend line (mechanized as close-and-next-open)

complexity.reason: needs a short-lookback trend-line projection and a break-then-reclaim state

notes: Grimes attributes the 1-3 bar trend-line concept to Al Brooks's 'Micro Trendlines' and Charles Drummond's Drummond Geometry; heavily overlapping the existing Brooks-derived MicroTrendLine* rules.

rejected.quote: Markets are fractal in nature, meaning that essentially the same patterns appear on all time frames
rejected.reason: background market-structure theory, no bar-level test

rejected.quote: The best option in most cases is to buy a little bit, wait so that you don't move the market too much, then buy some more, and repeat until the order is completely filled
rejected.reason: explains why the impulse/pullback pattern exists (order-execution theory), not itself a bar-level condition

rejected.quote: It is an axiom in technical analysis that the first entry in a trend is the best entry, but this is an example of the kind of hindsight analysis that must be avoided
rejected.reason: explicitly flagged by the author as non-actionable hindsight, not a forward-looking bar-level test

rejected.quote: Number of bars in each leg. This is a measure of time, and is usually redundant ... There is almost never any need to count bars
rejected.reason: author states this measure is redundant with slope/visual inspection; no independent bar-level test

rejected.quote: How can we build, refine, and verify the validity of our subjective analyses?
rejected.reason: methodological commentary on discretionary trading, no bar-level test

rejected.quote: many authors claim it is a self-fulfilling prophecy, as many traders are using the same tools and making the same decisions
rejected.reason: philosophical argument about why technical analysis works, no bar-level test

rejected.quote: are price levels skipped because large orders clear many levels in the book?
rejected.reason: requires order-book data the engine does not have

chapter_summary: Chapter 3 develops Grimes's fundamental impulse/pullback/impulse trend structure and works through how trends start (impulse legs confirmed by momentum-indicator extremes), how they run (winning vs. failing pullbacks, retracement depth, three pushes), and how they end (climaxes/parabolic moves, momentum divergence, Dow-theory trend-change rules, trend-line and channel relations, and swing-length/character warnings). It produced a large primitive family (Keltner-band tests, free bars, momentum-indicator extremes, swing/pivot-based pullback and trend-line candidates), several of which are depended on by Chapter 4's candidates (G03-11, G03-13, G03-17, G03-35); the trend-line/channel and three-pushes families overlap heavily with the existing Brooks-derived corpus, flagged throughout via likely_existing_rule.
